title: A method for ameliorating autoimmune disease by passive transfer of IVIg-primed leukocytes
protocol: Determine the volume of IVIg required based on experimental conditions and number of mice.
Remove a length of dialysis tubing (approximately 15-17 cm) and rinse in distilled H₂O.
Transfer the desired volume of IVIg or BSA solution into dialysis tube, tie the ends, and transfer to sterile beaker containing sterile PBS (pH 7.2).
Stir in a beaker overnight at 4°C.
Remove spleens from appropriate mice and mechanically disrupt in 5 mL of culture medium.
Filter disrupted spleen through a 70-μm nylon cell strainer.
Lose RBC using 1 mL of ACK buffer for 5 min.
Wash cells twice in RPMI-1640.
Purify CD11c+ and CD11c- cell fractions from splenic leukocytes by magnetic separation according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Disrupt spleen in RPMI-1640 containing 43 U/mL collagenase IV for 20 minutes at 37°C.
Further disrupt the spleen and add EDTA to a final concentration of 1 mM for 5 minutes at 37°C.
Filter the spleen preparation through a 70 μm nylon cell strainer.
Wash splenic leukocytes with CD11c purification buffer.
Resuspend the splenic leukocytes in CD11c purification buffer to a density of 2x10^8 nucleated cells/mL and incubate with CD11c-PE at 15 μL/mL for 15 minutes at 22°C.
Wash the splenic leukocytes after incubation.
Incubate the washed splenic leukocytes in PE selection cocktail at 100 μL cocktail/mL of cells for 15 minutes at 22°C.
Add magnetic particles at a concentration of 50 μL/mL cells and incubate for 10 minutes at 22°C, followed by separation using a magnet.
Collect the supernatant as the CD11c- cell fraction.
Remove the tube from the magnet and resuspend the remaining cells as the CD11c+ fraction.
Wash the CD11c+ fraction once in RPMI-1640.
Prepare single-cell suspensions by disrupting the spleen in RPMI-1640 and filtering through a 70 μm nylon cell strainer for both CD11b+ and CD11b- cell preparations.
Liberate red blood cells using ACK buffer and wash the resulting cells with RPMI-1640.
Resuspend cells at a density of 10^8/mL in CD11b purification buffer containing CD11b microbeads at a ratio of 10 μL/10^7 cells.
Incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the cells in CD11b purification buffer.
Apply the washed cells to a MACS column.
Collect the effluent as the CD11b- cell fraction.
Remove the column from the magnet and flush the cells from the column as the CD11b+ fraction.
Incubate splenic leukocytes (1.4x10^6/mL) with 18 mg/mL IVIg or BSA for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash cells twice in RPMI-1640.
Resuspend cells in culture medium to a concentration of 5x10^6/mL.
Incubate splenic leukocytes (2x10^7/mL) with antibody 2.4G2 (2.5 μg/mL) or normal rat IgG (2.5 μg/mL) for 15 min at 22°C in culture medium.
Wash cells once in RPMI-1640.
Incubate cells (2x10^7/mL) with goat F(ab')2 anti-rat IgG (25 μg/mL) for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash cells twice in RPMI-1640.
Resuspend cells in culture medium to a concentration of 5x10^6/mL.
Incubate splenic leukocytes (4x10^6/mL) with antibody 6C1 (10 μg/mL) or normal rat IgG (10 μg/mL) for 15 min at 22°C in culture medium.
Wash cells once in RPMI-1640.
Incubate cells (4x10^6/mL) with goat F(ab')2 anti-rat IgG (25 μg/mL) for 30 min at 37°C.
Dissolve OVA in PBS, pH 7.2 at a concentration of 5 mg/mL.
Incubate 1 mg of ovalbumin with 50 μg monoclonal anti-ovalbumin or normal mouse IgG for 30 min at 22°C to prepare soluble immune complexes (sIC).
Incubate splenic leukocytes at a concentration of 5x10^6/mL with sIC for 30 min at 37°C.
Wash the cells twice in RPMI-1640.
Resuspend the washed cells in culture medium to achieve a concentration of 5x10^6/mL.
Inject 200 μL of cell suspension (5x10^6/mL) into the tail vein of recipient mice on Day 0.
Inject each mouse intraperitoneally with 2 μg anti-platelet antibody (MWReg30) in 200 μL PBS, pH 7.2 on Day 1.
Bleed mice on Day 2 for platelet enumeration as described.
